quranic_mention: Named repeatedly beside Ibrahim and Ya'qub, yet the Quran narrates no episode of his life beyond the announcement of his birth
teaser: Announced to a woman who struck her own face in disbelief at the news. The Quran tells us almost nothing else about him — and honours him in more than a dozen places.

layers.title: Who
layers.subtitle: A prophet announced by angels to a childless couple already grown old.
layers.source: Ibn Kathir, Stories of the Prophets
layers.content:
Ishaq, peace be upon him, enters the Quran as news delivered to guests' hosts. The angels who were on their way to the towns of Lut stopped first at Ibrahim's tent. He brought them a roasted calf; they did not eat; he grew uneasy. They told him not to fear, and then: «وَامْرَأَتُهُ قَائِمَةٌ فَضَحِكَتْ فَبَشَّرْنَاهَا بِإِسْحَاقَ وَمِن وَرَاءِ إِسْحَاقَ يَعْقُوبَ» — "And his wife was standing, and she laughed. Then We gave her good tidings of Ishaq, and after Ishaq, Ya'qub." (Quran 11:71)

Two generations promised in a single sentence, before the first had been conceived.

Her reaction is preserved without editing: «قَالَتْ يَا وَيْلَتَىٰ أَأَلِدُ وَأَنَا عَجُوزٌ وَهَذَا بَعْلِي شَيْخًا إِنَّ هَذَا لَشَيْءٌ عَجِيبٌ» — "Woe to me! Shall I give birth while I am an old woman, and this, my husband, is an old man? This is an amazing thing." (Quran 11:72) Surah adh-Dhariyat records the same moment physically: «فَأَقْبَلَتِ امْرَأَتُهُ فِي صَرَّةٍ فَصَكَّتْ وَجْهَهَا وَقَالَتْ عَجُوزٌ عَقِيمٌ» — she came forward with a cry, struck her own face, and said: a barren old woman! (Quran 51:29)

The Quran does not give her name. Ibn Kathir supplies it as Sarah from the transmitted reports, and it is worth noticing which of the two sources is which. Ibrahim's own words on receiving both his sons carry no explanation, only gratitude: «الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ الَّذِي وَهَبَ لِي عَلَى الْكِبَرِ إِسْمَاعِيلَ وَإِسْحَاقَ إِنَّ رَبِّي لَسَمِيعُ الدُّعَاءِ» — praise be to Allah who granted me, in old age, Isma'il and Ishaq; indeed my Lord is the Hearer of supplication (Quran 14:39).

layers.title: The Call
layers.subtitle: A prophet whose message the Quran names through the mouth of his grandson.
layers.source: Ibn Kathir, Stories of the Prophets
layers.content:
Allah states his office plainly: «وَبَشَّرْنَاهُ بِإِسْحَاقَ نَبِيًّا مِّنَ الصَّالِحِينَ» — "And We gave him good tidings of Ishaq, a prophet from among the righteous." (Quran 37:112) He was announced as a prophet before he was born.

What did he preach? The Quran answers this indirectly, and the indirect route is itself instructive. In an Egyptian prison, his grandson Yusuf tells two fellow prisoners the name of the religion he follows: «وَاتَّبَعْتُ مِلَّةَ آبَائِي إِبْرَاهِيمَ وَإِسْحَاقَ وَيَعْقُوبَ مَا كَانَ لَنَا أَن نُّشْرِكَ بِاللَّهِ مِن شَيْءٍ» — "And I have followed the way of my fathers, Ibrahim, Ishaq and Ya'qub. It was not for us to associate anything with Allah." (Quran 12:38) That is the content of Ishaq's call, testified to by a descendant two generations down: uncompromised tawhid, transmitted intact.

Surah Sad gives Allah's own reference for him, grouped with his father and his son: «وَاذْكُرْ عِبَادَنَا إِبْرَاهِيمَ وَإِسْحَاقَ وَيَعْقُوبَ أُولِي الْأَيْدِي وَالْأَبْصَارِ» — remember Our servants Ibrahim, Ishaq and Ya'qub, possessors of strength and vision (Quran 38:45). Then the reason they were selected: «إِنَّا أَخْلَصْنَاهُمْ بِخَالِصَةٍ ذِكْرَى الدَّارِ» — We chose them for a purely sincere purpose: the remembrance of the Hereafter (Quran 38:46). And the verdict: «وَإِنَّهُمْ عِندَنَا لَمِنَ الْمُصْطَفَيْنَ الْأَخْيَارِ» — with Us they are among the chosen and the outstanding (Quran 38:47).

Strength, vision, and a mind fixed on the Home that comes after this one. That is the whole job description, and Allah considered it sufficient.

layers.title: The Trial
layers.subtitle: The waiting that preceded him, and the warning written into his blessing.
layers.source: Ibn Kathir, Stories of the Prophets
layers.content:
The trial recorded in his story is not a persecution. It is a wait, and it belonged to his parents before it belonged to him. Ibrahim had grown old calling people to Allah with no son from this wife at all. When the news finally arrived, it did not land as joy — it landed as impossibility. She struck her face and named herself: a barren old woman (Quran 51:29).

The angels' correction is one of the most bracing lines in the Quran: «قَالُوا أَتَعْجَبِينَ مِنْ أَمْرِ اللَّهِ» — "Do you wonder at the decree of Allah?" (Quran 11:73) And then, so that no one mistakes the source: «كَذَلِكِ قَالَ رَبُّكِ إِنَّهُ هُوَ الْحَكِيمُ الْعَلِيمُ» — thus has your Lord said; indeed He is the Wise, the Knowing (Quran 51:30).

The second trial is stranger, and it is attached to the blessing itself. Immediately after announcing Ishaq's birth, Allah says: «وَبَارَكْنَا عَلَيْهِ وَعَلَىٰ إِسْحَاقَ وَمِن ذُرِّيَّتِهِمَا مُحْسِنٌ وَظَالِمٌ لِّنَفْسِهِ مُّبِينٌ» — "And We blessed him and Ishaq. And among their descendants is the doer of good and the clearly unjust to himself." (Quran 37:113)

The blessing arrives with a disclaimer inside it. Allah tells Ishaq's father, in the same breath as the good news, that this line will produce both the righteous and the openly wrongdoing. No lineage in the Quran is granted immunity, and this is the verse that says so.

Of his household after that, Ibn Kathir is careful. He notes that the Quran does not give the details of Ishaq's life, and what he then reports — the choosing of his wife from his father's kin, the birth of twin sons, the quarrel between them — he attributes to commentators and, for most of the detail, explicitly to the People of the Book. He does not upgrade it. Neither will we.

layers.title: The Sign
layers.subtitle: The miracle was not something he did. It was that he existed at all.
layers.source: Ibn Kathir, Stories of the Prophets
layers.content:
Some prophets were given a staff, a she-camel, a ship. Ishaq was given nothing, because Ishaq was the sign.

The angels described the promised child twice with the same word: «وَبَشَّرُوهُ بِغُلَامٍ عَلِيمٍ» — "and they gave him good tidings of a learned boy." (Quran 51:28) In Surah al-Hijr: «إِنَّا نُبَشِّرُكَ بِغُلَامٍ عَلِيمٍ» (Quran 15:53). Not merely a boy: a boy who would know.

Surah al-Anbiya adds a detail that changes how the gift should be read: «وَوَهَبْنَا لَهُ إِسْحَاقَ وَيَعْقُوبَ نَافِلَةً وَكُلًّا جَعَلْنَا صَالِحِينَ» — "And We gave him Ishaq and Ya'qub as an additional gift, and all of them We made righteous." (Quran 21:72) نَافِلَةً — an extra, beyond the request. Ibrahim had asked for a righteous child and already had Isma'il. Ishaq and Ya'qub were given over and above the answer.

And Surah Maryam attaches the gift to a moment: «فَلَمَّا اعْتَزَلَهُمْ وَمَا يَعْبُدُونَ مِن دُونِ اللَّهِ وَهَبْنَا لَهُ إِسْحَاقَ وَيَعْقُوبَ وَكُلًّا جَعَلْنَا نَبِيًّا» — "So when he had left them and what they worshipped besides Allah, We gave him Ishaq and Ya'qub, and each of them We made a prophet." (Quran 19:49)

Read the order. He walked away from his father, his town, and its gods, and lost the family he had. Then he was given a family that produced prophets. The next verse completes it: «وَوَهَبْنَا لَهُم مِّن رَّحْمَتِنَا وَجَعَلْنَا لَهُمْ لِسَانَ صِدْقٍ عَلِيًّا» — and We gave them of Our mercy, and made for them a high tongue of truth (Quran 19:50). Ibn Kathir explains the last phrase as lasting, honourable remembrance on the tongues of people. Every Muslim who names Ishaq in a prayer is that verse still operating.

layers.title: The Legacy
layers.subtitle: Prophethood and scripture were placed in his line — and it guaranteed no one.
layers.source: Ibn Kathir, Stories of the Prophets
layers.content:
His inheritance is stated as an institutional fact: «وَوَهَبْنَا لَهُ إِسْحَاقَ وَيَعْقُوبَ وَجَعَلْنَا فِي ذُرِّيَّتِهِ النُّبُوَّةَ وَالْكِتَابَ» — "And We gave him Ishaq and Ya'qub, and placed in his descendants prophethood and the Scripture." (Quran 29:27) From this line came Ya'qub, Yusuf, Musa, Harun, Dawud, Sulayman, Zakariyya, Yahya and Isa. The Torah, the Zabur and the Injil all descend through it.

So a Muslim's belief is not optional here. «قُولُوا آمَنَّا بِاللَّهِ وَمَا أُنزِلَ إِلَيْنَا وَمَا أُنزِلَ إِلَىٰ إِبْرَاهِيمَ وَإِسْمَاعِيلَ وَإِسْحَاقَ وَيَعْقُوبَ وَالْأَسْبَاطِ» — say: we believe in Allah, and what was revealed to us, and what was revealed to Ibrahim, Isma'il, Ishaq, Ya'qub and the descendants — and the verse ends «لَا نُفَرِّقُ بَيْنَ أَحَدٍ مِّنْهُمْ», we make no distinction between any of them (Quran 2:136). Ya'qub is told by Allah, through Yusuf's story, that the favour on him completes what was completed «عَلَىٰ أَبَوَيْكَ مِنْ قَبْلُ إِبْرَاهِيمَ وَإِسْحَاقَ» (Quran 12:6).

And then the correction that keeps all of it from becoming tribalism. Quran 37:113 says the descendants of Ibrahim and Ishaq include the doer of good and the one plainly wronging himself. Ibn Kathir's reading is unsentimental: honour ran in the line, but salvation never did. Being descended from Ishaq entitled no one to anything.

There is one more legacy, and it is a discipline rather than a doctrine. Long, detailed biographies of Ishaq exist outside the Quran. Ibn Kathir handles them by labelling every strand — this from the commentators, this from the People of the Book — and by stating outright that the Quran gives no details of his life. He leaves the gap visible instead of closing it. A reader who learns that habit from Ishaq's entry has taken away more than a story.

quiz.prompt: How did Ibrahim's wife react when the angels announced the birth of Ishaq?

options.text: She prostrated in thanks
She laughed, then cried out and struck her own face, calling herself a barren old woman
She asked for the news in writing
She left the tent without speaking

quiz.citation: Quran 11:71-72 and Quran 51:29 — «فَصَكَّتْ وَجْهَهَا وَقَالَتْ عَجُوزٌ عَقِيمٌ»
quiz.scholar_reflection: The Quran preserves the shock rather than tidying it. The angels answered not by arguing with her body but by relocating the question: «أَتَعْجَبِينَ مِنْ أَمْرِ اللَّهِ».

quiz.prompt: What did Allah say about the descendants of Ibrahim and Ishaq in the same passage that announces the blessing on them?

options.text: That all of them would be prophets
That they would rule the earth
That among them is the doer of good and the one clearly unjust to himself
That they would never be tested

quiz.citation: Quran 37:113 — «وَمِن ذُرِّيَّتِهِمَا مُحْسِنٌ وَظَالِمٌ لِّنَفْسِهِ مُّبِينٌ»
quiz.scholar_reflection: The disclaimer is placed inside the blessing itself. No lineage in the Quran is granted immunity, and this is the verse that establishes it.

quiz.prompt: According to Quran 19:49, when was Ibrahim given Ishaq and Ya'qub?

options.text: Before he began calling his people
After he had withdrawn from his people and what they worshipped besides Allah
While he was still living in his father's house
After he settled in Makkah

quiz.citation: Quran 19:49 — «فَلَمَّا اعْتَزَلَهُمْ وَمَا يَعْبُدُونَ مِن دُونِ اللَّهِ وَهَبْنَا لَهُ إِسْحَاقَ وَيَعْقُوبَ»
quiz.scholar_reflection: He lost the family he was born into and was given a family that produced prophets. The Quran places the loss before the gift and lets the reader draw the line.

quiz.prompt: Where in the Quran do we learn the content of Ishaq's religion?

options.text: From a long sermon of his recorded in Surah Hud
From his grandson Yusuf, speaking in prison, who names the way of Ibrahim, Ishaq and Ya'qub as pure tawhid
From a scripture revealed to him and quoted in full
The Quran does not connect him to any teaching

quiz.citation: Quran 12:38 — «وَاتَّبَعْتُ مِلَّةَ آبَائِي إِبْرَاهِيمَ وَإِسْحَاقَ وَيَعْقُوبَ»
quiz.scholar_reflection: The proof that his call was transmitted intact is not a document but a descendant, in a prison cell, refusing shirk two generations later.

quiz.prompt: How does Ibn Kathir handle the detailed accounts of Ishaq's marriage and household?

options.text: He states that the Quran gives no details of Ishaq's life, and attributes the accounts to commentators and to the People of the Book
He presents them as established hadith
He rejects Ishaq's prophethood over them
He claims they are from Surah as-Saffat

quiz.citation: Ibn Kathir, Stories of the Prophets — chapter on Ishaq
quiz.scholar_reflection: He labels each strand rather than blending them, and leaves the gap in the record visible. Marking the grade of a report honestly is part of transmitting it.

quiz.prompt: «أَتَعْجَبِينَ مِنْ أَمْرِ اللَّهِ» — do you wonder at the decree of Allah? Which good outcome in your life do you privately consider closed?

options.text: Marriage, or children
A career or calling I think I have aged out of
A relative I have given up hope of ever seeing change
My own reform — I have decided this is simply who I am

quiz.scholar_reflection: She was not rebuked for feeling it. She was moved off her own arithmetic and onto Allah's. The question is not whether your calculation is correct; it is whether it is the final word.
quiz.slider_label: How closed have you decided it is?

quiz.prompt: Ishaq and Ya'qub are called نَافِلَةً — a gift beyond what was asked for. What in your life arrived that you never asked for?

options.text: A person who changed my direction
A door that opened after a different one closed
A hardship that turned out to be a protection
I have never sat down long enough to notice

quiz.scholar_reflection: Ibrahim asked for one righteous child. He was answered, and then given two prophets on top of the answer. Most gratitude fails not from denial but from never auditing the surplus.
quiz.slider_label: How much of your life was unrequested?

quiz.prompt: Allah's stated reason for choosing Ibrahim, Ishaq and Ya'qub was ذِكْرَى الدَّارِ — remembrance of the Hereafter. How often does the Hereafter actually enter your decisions?

options.text: In worship, but rarely in money or work decisions
When I am afraid or grieving, then it fades
As a background belief that does not move my calendar
It is the frame I decide inside, most of the time

quiz.scholar_reflection: The verse pairs it with أُولِي الْأَيْدِي وَالْأَبْصَارِ — strength and vision. Remembering the Home was not a withdrawal from work; it was what made their work worth recording.
quiz.slider_label: How present is the Hereafter in your week?

quiz.prompt: Descent from a prophet secured nothing for Ishaq's line. What inherited religious credit are you living on?

options.text: A family known for its practice
A country, madhhab or movement I was born into
Religious knowledge I acquired years ago and stopped adding to
None, and that is uncomfortable to sit with

quiz.scholar_reflection: Allah put the warning inside the blessing so the two would never be separated. An inheritance can start a person's deen; the Quran refuses to let it finish it.
quiz.slider_label: How much is inherited, how much earned?

quiz.prompt: The Quran narrates almost nothing of Ishaq's life, and honours him more than a dozen times. What would it change if your work were never narrated?

options.text: I would do noticeably less of it
I would do the same things with less energy
I would probably do better work
I do not know, and that uncertainty is the answer

quiz.scholar_reflection: Allah gave him a lasting, honourable remembrance without giving him a biography. The record that matters was never the one written by people, and Ishaq's entry in the Quran proves the two are not the same document.
quiz.slider_label: How much of your effort needs an audience?
